summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent ER-positive breast cancer and idiopathic gastroparesis presented with a severe flare of nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain. Initial evaluation revealed hypovolemia and metabolic abnormalities consistent with starvation ketosis, which resolved with IV hydration and supportive care. A CT scan showed new hepatic and skeletal lesions suspicious for metastatic disease, prompting a percutaneous liver biopsy. She was managed for gastroparesis with antiemetics and dietary advancement, and a UTI with E. coli was incidentally detected and treated. The Denosumab was held pending oncology review. She improved clinically, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home with plans to follow up with her oncologist for biopsy results and further management.
problems: Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct
Malignant neoplasm of unspecified site of unspecified female breast
